name: Thomas Silva
life: “I still remember rocking a borrowed pram with my ankle.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Thomas keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I hear the dryers through my pillow. I want one morning when the neighbors sing with them.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a red windbreaker and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Thomas has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Thomas touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Thomas finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To agree one undisturbed morning with the singers.
family: Quinn Laurent is Thomas’s older cousin. Thomas calls about good news first. Quinn is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The day sailor's divorce*, Quinn says, “I kept hearing who paid most. I brought the maintenance log with everyone's cold hands in it.”
connections: Franklin Brandt. The people trying to sleep get a say in when the morning choir rehearses.

reactions.situation: The washer bearing goes quiet mid-song
reactions.response: Thomas listens for the missing note and lets maintenance know what changed.

reactions.response: Thomas keeps listening through the pause and lets the musician choose the next note.
